title: Compact tiling with priority profiles and KV-aware density for virtual tables
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Large result sets cause chaotic column layouts and jarring reflows in Redwood Console. Current density toggles (compact/comfortable) are global and often either waste horizontal space or clip important columns. We need a system that: 1) collapses low-priority columns automatically in narrow or high-cardinality views, 2) surfaces inline aggregations and context pills to preserve information density, and 3) cooperates with runtime KV/prefix caching heuristics to avoid expensive re-render cost during scroll/seek. This ticket proposes a design spec for a compact tiling mode driven by per-column priority profiles and a KV-aware density fallback that gracefully degrades to a medium-density view when cache misses or network latency exceed thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens and spacing rules updated for a new 'compact-tiling' density variant with token names matching the system conventions
Interaction spec for priority-driven column collapse: explicit pinning, automatic collapse order, and override affordances documented
Accessible keyboard flows defined for toggling collapsed columns and reading collapsed column summaries via screen readers
Figma prototype demonstrating 3 dataset sizes (sparse, medium, dense) with compact-tiling enabled and clear collapse animations
Developer handoff doc with example JSON column profile schema and recommended defaults for common datatypes
Integration plan showing how KV/cache miss signals (from runtime) will toggle medium-density fallback and sample UI states for slow-path
Performance checklist with target metrics: no >8% increase in average frame render cost for dense datasets vs current compact, and measured UX latency under simulated KV miss conditions
notes: Design rationale: prioritize content readability over strict column preservation for dense tables; surface aggregates inline so users rarely need to expand every column
We want to avoid surprises for power users—explicit pin and uncollapse affordances remain prominent and persistent per-user
Trade-offs discussed: aggressive collapse reduces horizontal scrolling but increases vertical stacking for multi-line cells; opted for a two-line cell clamp + tooltip instead of full wrapping
Accessibility: need ARIA announcements when auto-collapse occurs during resize or dynamic dataset changes; initial wording drafted in ARIA section
Naming guidance: 'compact-tiling' chosen to distinguish from existing 'compact' token set; tokens: spacing.compactTiling.*
Column profile schema draft: ['id', 'label', 'priority:int', 'minWidth:int', 'preferredWidth:int', 'aggregations:list', 'collapseBehavior:string'] — to be refined with eng
KV-aware fallback: runtime will emit an event 'inference.kv_latency' or 'cache.miss-rate' — UX will display a subtle density toast and auto-switch to 'medium-tiling' until metric stabilizes
